title: What Every Music Company Made in Q2 2026 (Updating)
summary: From Live Nation to UMG to SiriusXM, a roundup of what the biggest publicly traded music companies have reported so far for the quarter ending June 30.
body: Around a dozen publicly traded music companies are reporting earnings in the weeks stretching from late July into August — and early results show that from the major labels to music streamers, satellite radio to live events, consumers are still spending on music. On the label front, as of July 31, both Universal Music Group (UMG) and Sony Music both showed solid results, with overall revenue at the latter surging by 20% year-over-year. In Korea, HYBE saw strong results in the second quarter from K-pop supergroup BTS ‘ world tour and sales of its fifth studio album, ARIRANG. title: Tom Corson Named COO at Warner Music Group
summary: The executive, who succeeds Armin Zerza in the role, has served as co-chairman and COO at Warner Records since 2018.
body: Warner Records co-chairman and COO Tom Corson was promoted to COO of the larger Warner Music Group (WMG), succeeding Armin Zerza in the role, the company announced on Friday (July 31). Corson has served as co-chairman and COO of Warner Records, where he led business operations, strategy and commercial development, since 2018. During that time, he’s succeeded in growing the label and its artists, which include Madonna, Red Hot Chili Peppers, Dua Lipa, Zach Bryan, Benson Boone, Michael Bublé, Teddy Swims, Linkin Park, Cody Johnson, and Sombr. Warner Records finished in fifth place in label market share at midyear , notching a 5.11% mark. Related Warner Music Group CFO & COO Armin Zerza Steps Down After One Year Glenn A. title: NASA’s Roman Telescope to Carry 1.35 Million Names to Deep Space
summary: On July 27, technicians at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida installed a memory card containing 1,350,144 names as part of a commemorative plaque on the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. The names were submitted by people globally, including astronauts from Artemis II and Artemis III. The mem…
body: On July 27, technicians at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida installed a memory card containing 1,350,144 names as part of a commemorative plaque on the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. The names were submitted by people globally, including astronauts from Artemis II and Artemis III. The memory card will travel with the Roman observatory to the Sun-Earth Lagrange point 2, or L2, about one million miles from Earth, where the Sun’s and Earth’s gravity balance out. Roman is named after Dr. Nancy Grace Roman, NASA’s first chief astronomer and one of the architects of the agency’s modern science program. Roman championed space-based observatories that could study the universe from above Earth’s hazy atmosphere while making their data broadly available to the scientific community. NASA and SpaceX are targeting launch for no earlier than 7:26 a.m. EDT Sunday, Aug. 30 aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy. To learn more about the Roman mission, visit: https://www.nasa.gov/roman Image credit: NASA/Jolearra Tshiteya
